sources.entry: pyarmor - A tool used to obfuscate Python scripts, bind obfuscated scripts to a fixed machine or expire obfuscated scripts.

summary.one_liner: Pyarmor is a command-line tool that obfuscates Python scripts, binds them to specific machines, and sets expiration dates on them.
summary.what_it_does: Pyarmor obfuscates Python scripts so the output remains a standard .py file that can replace the original. Per the README, it renames functions, methods, classes, variables and arguments, and can convert some Python functions to C functions compiled into machine instructions for stronger obfuscation. It can bind obfuscated scripts to specific machines or set expiration dates on them. The README also mentions Themida protection on Windows. The quick start shows `pyarmor gen foo.py` writing an obfuscated file to dist/foo.py that calls a pyarmor_runtime helper on load.
use_cases: protect source code from being read
bind a Python script to a specific machine
set an expiration date on a Python program
add Themida protection to Python on Windows
notable: Obfuscated output stays as standard .py files that can replace originals
Can compile some functions to C and then machine code for irreversible obfuscation
Machine binding and expiration dates for obfuscated scripts
Supports Python 2 and 3 on Windows, Linux, and Apple Intel and Silicon macOS
caveats: Distributed as shareware; the free trial version has some limitations (README says it never expires)
Some features are exclusive to Python 3 or to specific architectures
